imageRegistry.description: Registry override applied to every image reference in the umbrella (read by the vendored `common` library chart's `common.images.image` helper)

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull secrets applied to every workload in the umbrella (same helper as above)

storageClass.description: Default StorageClass for any PVC in the umbrella (a convention from the vendored `common` library chart; this chart renders no PVC template itself, so currently unused here)

_topics.description: Kafka topics shared across every chart instance in an umbrella; merged into each instance's own `_topics` below (kafkaTopicsParameters)

commandPrefix.description: Path prefix prepended to `executable` before it's rendered into `command`/`args`

commandStyle.description: "shell": wrap executable+args in `command` via a shell string (needs a shell in the image). "exec": render command=[prefixed executable], args as a real argv list - for shell-less hardened runtime images.

executable.description: Executable name and arguments (will be combined into a shell command)

enabled.description: Render the Deployment resource; disable for Job/CronJob-only charts
Render a one-off Job resource alongside (or instead of) the Deployment

cronjobs.description:
A map of CronJobs to render alongside (or instead of) the Deployment. It's a map rather than a list so downstream values files can override a single cronjob's fields (e.g. `cronjobs.cleanup.schedule`) without having to redefine the whole list - Helm only deep-merges maps, not lists.
The map key also becomes a suffix on the CronJob's name (`<fullname>-<key>`), except for the reserved key `default`, which renders with no suffix - use that key for the common case of a single cronjob.
Each entry may override `schedule`, `successfulJobsHistoryLimit`, `executable`, and `executableArgs` independently of the Deployment/other cronjobs; unset fields fall back to the top-level values.
`podAnnotations` on an entry are added on top of the top-level `podAnnotations` (and any vault agent annotations), taking precedence on conflicting keys - e.g. to set `vault.hashicorp.com/agent-pre-populate-only: "true"` only for a cronjob while the Deployment keeps the vault agent sidecar running.

nameOverride.description: Override just the chart-name portion of generated resource names (the vendored `common` library chart's `common.names.name` convention)

fullnameOverride.description: Override the entire generated resource name, bypassing the `<release>-<chart>` convention (the vendored `common` library chart's `common.names.fullname`)

namespaceOverride.description: Override the namespace resources render into instead of `.Release.Namespace` (the vendored `common` library chart's `common.names.namespace`)

annotations.description: Extra annotations added to the Deployment/CronJob/Job/HTTPRoute/Probe resources' own metadata (narrower reach than commonAnnotations below)

labels.description: Extra labels added to the same resources' own metadata (narrower reach than commonLabels below)

commonLabels.description: Labels merged onto nearly every rendered resource's metadata (Deployment, CronJob, Job, Service, HPA, DestinationRule, HTTPRoute, Probe)

commonAnnotations.description: Annotations merged onto the same broad set of resources as commonLabels

registry.description: Default image registry; overridden by global.imageRegistry when set

repository.description: Image repository path (create_charts.py fills this in per member)

tag.description: Image tag; left empty so it falls back to the chart's appVersion == the platform version (ADR-0004)

digest.description: Pin the image by digest instead of tag, when set (takes precedence in the vendored `common` library chart's `common.images.image` helper)

pullPolicy.description: imagePullPolicy override; null defaults to Always for a `latest` tag, IfNotPresent otherwise

pullSecrets.description: Extra pull secrets for just this image reference

replicaCount.description: Deployment replica count; ignored when autoscaling.enabled

revisionHistoryLimit.description: Number of old ReplicaSets Kubernetes keeps around for rollback

shareProcessNamespace.description: Share the pod's process namespace across containers; forced true whenever vaultAgent.enabled (the agent sends signals to the app's PID)

fsGroup.description: Group ID Kubernetes chowns mounted volumes to

initContainers.description: Extra init containers to run before the main container (the migration init container below is prepended to this list when enabled)

enabled.description: Run a dedicated init container for DB migrations before the main container starts

image.description: Image for the migration init container; defaults to the main container's image when empty

executable.description: Executable name and arguments run inside the migration init container

env.description: Extra env vars for just the migration init container

volumeMounts.description: Extra volume mounts for just the migration init container (on top of the shared volumeMounts every container gets)

podLabels.description: Labels applied only to the Pod template (Deployment/CronJob/Job pod spec), distinct from `labels`/`commonLabels` on the parent resource

podAnnotations.description: Annotations applied only to the Pod template; combined with any Vault Agent annotations when vaultAgent.enabled

podAffinityPreset.description: Pod-affinity preset name (e.g. "soft"/"hard"), from the vendored `common` library chart; empty disables it

podAntiAffinityPreset.description: Pod-anti-affinity preset name (vendored `common` library chart convention); "soft" spreads replicas across nodes when possible

type.description: Node-affinity preset type ("soft"/"hard"), from the vendored `common` library chart; empty disables it

affinity.description: Raw Kubernetes affinity spec; overrides all three presets above when set

nodeSelector.description: Plain node-selector labels for pod scheduling

priorityClassName.description: PriorityClass to schedule the pod with

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period before SIGKILL on pod termination

podRestartPolicy.description: Pod-level restart policy for the Deployment (Jobs/CronJobs set their own, ignoring this)

containerPorts.description: Container ports, name -> port (bare number = TCP; {port, protocol} for anything else). Also the single source the Service's and NetworkPolicy's own `ports:` are derived from - a Service always exposes exactly what its container listens on here, so there's one map to keep in sync, not several. A map, not a list, so an overlay can add/override one named port without repeating the rest. Empty = no ports declared anywhere.

enabled.description: Render a container livenessProbe from this block (minus `enabled`)
Render a container readinessProbe from this block (minus `enabled`)
Render a container startupProbe from this block (minus `enabled`)
Render the container securityContext from this block (minus `enabled`)

extraVolumes.description: Extra volumes for the pod (on top of the config/kafka-secret volumes this chart already renders)

extraVolumeMounts.description: Extra volume mounts for the main container (on top of the shared ones every container gets)

sidecars.description: Extra full container specs appended alongside the main container

envVars.description: Extra literal env vars for the main container (the generated CONFIG_YAML env var is appended to this list when configMap.envVar.enabled)

envVarsConfigMap.description: Name of a ConfigMap to load as bulk env vars via `envFrom`

envVarsSecret.description: Name of a Secret to load as bulk env vars via `envFrom`

enabled.description: Render the Service resource

create.description: Create a dedicated ServiceAccount for this release

enabled.description: Render a HorizontalPodAutoscaler targeting the Deployment

targetCPU.description: Target average CPU utilization percentage; omit/empty to skip this metric

targetMemory.description: Target average memory utilization percentage; omit/empty to skip this metric

metrics.description: Extra raw HPA metric entries appended after CPU/memory

topicPrefix.description: Prefix prepended to every Kafka topic name this chart renders/references

_topics.description: Per-instance Kafka topics this chart owns (merged with global._topics); shape is {<key>: {topic: {name, value}, type: {name, value}, types: [...]}} - see kafkaTopicsParameters/kafkaUser below for how each field is consumed

_consumerGroup.description: ACL entry (or entries) granting this chart's consumer group access, rendered onto the KafkaUser resource when kafkaUser.enabled

kafkaTopicsParameters.description: Fold `_topics`/`_consumerGroup` into the rendered config.yaml as service config parameters (topic name/type env vars); set false to render topics for KafkaUser ACLs only, without also injecting them as config

enabled.description: Render a Strimzi KafkaUser (TLS cert + ACLs from _topics/_consumerGroup)

caCertSecretName.description: Secret holding the Kafka cluster's CA cert, mounted alongside the user's own TLS secret

dbName.description: Database name; combined with dbNamePrefix and injected into config.yaml as db_name. NOTE: mongodb.dbName is the fallback used when the top-level dbName (set per-member, not defaulted here) is empty

namespace.description: Together with mongodb.service.name and cluster.name, forms the Vault KV path this chart reads a dynamic MongoDB credential from

apiBasePath.description: Public API path prefix; combined with apiBasePathPrefix (set by an aliasing umbrella) and injected into config.yaml as api_root_path

serviceName.description: Logical service name; combined with serviceNamePrefix and injected into config.yaml as service_name

fromPodName.description: Inject a <CONFIG_PREFIX>_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID env var sourced from the Kubernetes Downward API (metadata.name), overriding config.service_instance_id per-pod. Env vars beat the YAML config file in hexkit config_from_yaml priority order, so this makes the value genuinely unique per replica instead of the static per-member string every service currently hardcodes in its own chart-values.yaml config block (which collides across replicas once replicaCount > 1, contradicting hexkit KafkaConfig.service_instance_id's own "uniquely identifies this instance" contract).

enabled.description: Render the ConfigMap holding config.yaml and mount it into the container
Also add a `<CONFIG_PREFIX>_CONFIG_YAML` env var pointing at mountPath

config.description: The service's own configuration payload (merged with the computed kafka/api/db/service-name values below into the rendered config.yaml)

mongo_dsn.description: MongoDB connection string. Might include credentials. For more information see: https://naiveskill.com/mongodb-connection-string/
mongo_dsn.title: Mongo Dsn

db_permissions.description: List of permissions that can be granted on a collection. Use * to signify 'all'. The format is '<db_name>.<collection_name>:<permissions>', e.g. 'db1.collection1.crud'. The permissions are 'r' for read and 'w' for write. '*' can be used to mean both read and write (or 'rw'). Deletion is a write operation. If db_permissions are not set, no operations are allowed on any database or collection.
db_permissions.title: Db Permissions

allow_empty_prefix.description: Only set to True for local testing. If False, `db_prefix` cannot be empty. This is to prevent accidental deletion of others' data in shared environments, i.e. staging.
allow_empty_prefix.title: Allow Empty Prefix

db_prefix.description: Prefix to add to all database names used in the SMS.
db_prefix.title: Db Prefix

token_hashes.description: List of token hashes corresponding to the tokens that can be used to authenticate calls to this service. Hashes are made with SHA-256.
token_hashes.title: Token Hashes

log_level.description: The minimum log level to capture.
log_level.title: Log Level

vault_path.description: Path without leading or trailing slashes where secrets should be stored in the vault.
vault_path.title: Vault Path

service_name.description: Short name of this service. NOTE: this chart's configmap.tpl always overwrites config.service_name with the value computed from `serviceName` - a value set directly under config.service_name is silently discarded. Set `serviceName` instead.
service_name.title: Service Name

service_instance_id.description: A string that uniquely identifies this instance across all instances of this service. This is included in log messages.
service_instance_id.title: Service Instance Id

kafka_servers.description: A list of connection strings to connect to Kafka bootstrap servers.
kafka_servers.title: Kafka Servers

kafka_security_protocol.description: Protocol used to communicate with brokers. Valid values are: PLAINTEXT, SSL.
kafka_security_protocol.title: Kafka Security Protocol

kafka_ssl_cafile.description: Certificate Authority file path containing certificates used to sign broker certificates. If a CA is not specified, the default system CA will be used if found by OpenSSL.
kafka_ssl_cafile.title: Kafka Ssl Cafile

kafka_ssl_certfile.description: Optional filename of client certificate, as well as any CA certificates needed to establish the certificate's authenticity.
kafka_ssl_certfile.title: Kafka Ssl Certfile

kafka_ssl_keyfile.description: Optional filename containing the client private key.
kafka_ssl_keyfile.title: Kafka Ssl Keyfile

kafka_ssl_password.description: Optional password to be used for the client private key.
kafka_ssl_password.title: Kafka Ssl Password

generate_correlation_id.description: A flag, which, if False, will result in an error when inbound requests don't possess a correlation ID. If True, requests without a correlation ID will be assigned a newly generated ID in the correlation ID middleware function.
generate_correlation_id.title: Generate Correlation Id

kafka_max_message_size.description: The largest message size that can be transmitted, in bytes, before compression. Only services that have a need to send/receive larger messages should set this. When used alongside compression, this value can be set to something greater than the broker's `message.max.bytes` field, which effectively concerns the compressed message size.
kafka_max_message_size.title: Kafka Max Message Size

kafka_compression_type.description: The compression type used for messages. Valid values are: None, gzip, snappy, lz4, and zstd. If None, no compression is applied. This setting is only relevant for the producer and has no effect on the consumer. If set to a value, the producer will compress messages before sending them to the Kafka broker. If unsure, zstd provides a good balance between speed and compression ratio.
kafka_compression_type.title: Kafka Compression Type

kafka_max_retries.description: The maximum number of times to immediately retry consuming an event upon failure. Works independently of the dead letter queue.
kafka_max_retries.title: Kafka Max Retries

kafka_enable_dlq.description: A flag to toggle the dead letter queue. If set to False, the service will crash upon exhausting retries instead of publishing events to the DLQ. If set to True, the service will publish events to the DLQ topic after exhausting all retries
kafka_enable_dlq.title: Kafka Enable DLQ

kafka_dlq_topic.description: The name of the topic used to resolve error-causing events.
kafka_dlq_topic.title: Kafka DLQ Topic

kafka_retry_backoff.description: The number of seconds to wait before retrying a failed event. The backoff time is doubled for each retry attempt.
kafka_retry_backoff.title: Kafka Retry Backoff

vault_secrets_mount_point.description: Name used to address the secret engine under a custom mount path.
vault_secrets_mount_point.title: Vault Secrets Mount Point

vault_role_id.description: Vault role ID to access a specific prefix
vault_role_id.title: Vault Role Id

vault_secret_id.description: Vault secret ID to access a specific prefix
vault_secret_id.title: Vault Secret Id

vault_verify.description: SSL certificates (CA bundle) used to verify the identity of the vault, or True to use the default CAs, or False for no verification.
vault_verify.title: Vault Verify

vault_kube_role.description: Vault role name used for Kubernetes authentication
vault_kube_role.title: Vault Kube Role

vault_auth_mount_point.description: Adapter specific mount path for the corresponding auth backend. If none is provided, the default is used.
vault_auth_mount_point.title: Vault Auth Mount Point

service_account_token_path.description: Path to service account token used by kube auth adapter.
service_account_token_path.title: Service Account Token Path

mongo_timeout.description: Timeout in seconds for API calls to MongoDB. The timeout applies to all steps needed to complete the operation, including server selection, connection checkout, serialization, and server-side execution. When the timeout expires, PyMongo raises a timeout exception. If set to None, the operation will not time out (default MongoDB behavior).
mongo_timeout.title: Mongo Timeout

log_format.description: If set, will replace JSON formatting with the specified string format. If not set, has no effect. In addition to the standard attributes, the following can also be specified: timestamp, service, instance, level, correlation_id, and details
log_format.title: Log Format

log_traceback.description: Whether to include exception tracebacks in log messages.
log_traceback.title: Log Traceback

port.description: Port to expose the server on the specified host
port.title: Port

auto_reload.description: A development feature. Set to `True` to automatically reload the server upon code changes
auto_reload.title: Auto Reload

workers.description: Number of workers processes to run.
workers.title: Workers

timeout_keep_alive.description: The time in seconds to keep an idle connection open for subsequent requests before closing it. This value should be higher than the timeout used by any client or reverse proxy to avoid premature connection closures.
timeout_keep_alive.title: Timeout Keep Alive

api_root_path.description: Root path at which the API is reachable. This is relative to the specified host and port. NOTE: this chart's configmap.tpl always overwrites config.api_root_path with the value computed from `apiBasePath` - a value set directly under config.api_root_path is silently discarded. Set `apiBasePath` instead.
api_root_path.title: Api Root Path

openapi_url.description: Path to get the openapi specification in JSON format. This is relative to the specified host and port.
openapi_url.title: Openapi Url

docs_url.description: Path to host the swagger documentation. This is relative to the specified host and port.
docs_url.title: Docs Url

cors_allowed_origins.description: A list of origins that should be permitted to make cross-origin requests. By default, cross-origin requests are not allowed. You can use ['*'] to allow any origin.
cors_allowed_origins.title: Cors Allowed Origins

cors_allow_credentials.description: Indicate that cookies should be supported for cross-origin requests. Defaults to False. Also, cors_allowed_origins cannot be set to ['*'] for credentials to be allowed. The origins must be explicitly specified.
cors_allow_credentials.title: Cors Allow Credentials

cors_allowed_methods.description: A list of HTTP methods that should be allowed for cross-origin requests. Defaults to ['GET']. You can use ['*'] to allow all standard methods.
cors_allowed_methods.title: Cors Allowed Methods

cors_allowed_headers.description: A list of HTTP request headers that should be supported for cross-origin requests. Defaults to []. You can use ['*'] to allow all request headers. The Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Language, Content-Type and some are always allowed for CORS requests.
cors_allowed_headers.title: Cors Allowed Headers

cors_exposed_headers.description: A list of HTTP response headers that should be exposed for cross-origin responses. Defaults to []. Note that you can NOT use ['*'] to expose all response headers. The Cache-Control, Content-Language, Content-Length, Content-Type, Expires, Last-Modified and Pragma headers are always exposed for CORS responses.
cors_exposed_headers.title: Cors Exposed Headers
